record.paper_title: A note on the convergence of RED algorithms under minimal hypotheses and open questions
record.context_brief: When RED is theoretically preferable to GPGD
record.original_question: For inverse problems y = A x̂ + e with x̂ in a low-dimensional model set Σ, generalized projected gradient descent (GPGD) uses x_{n+1} = P_Σ(x_n) − μAᵀ(AP_Σ(x_n) − y) and can stably recover x̂ with a linear rate under restricted-isometry and restricted-Lipschitz hypotheses. Modified RED reduces to GPGD when λ = 1, while other admissible λ values are described as giving slower convergence and less identifiability; the classical RED convergence route also appears to require restrictive conditions. Under what theoretical setup would the use of a classical or modified RED scheme be warranted instead of GPGD, given that RED has worse convergence-rate and identifiability properties in the analyzed setting?

evidence.quote: the generalized projected gradient descent (GPGD) iterations xn+1 = PΣ(xn) − μAT(APΣ(xn) − y) stably recover x̂ with linear rate
To the best of our knowledge, the RIP and restricted Lipschitz constants are the weakest known hypotheses leading to such convergence guarantees.

We see that if we chose λ = 1, we fall on GPGD iterations and obtain the same convergence rate with modified RED (under the additional orthogonality assumption of the projection). Other admissible λ lead to slower convergence (and less identifiability).

Given the results of the previous Section, what theoretical set-up would warrant the use of a (classical or modified) RED scheme instead of GPGD as convergence rates and identifiability properties are worse than GPGD?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let A : R^N → R^m be a linear measurement operator and consider the inverse problem y = A x̂ + e, where x̂ belongs to a (possibly nonconvex) low-dimensional model set Σ ⊂ R^N and e ∈ R^m is a noise vector. Let P_Σ : R^N → Σ denote a (not necessarily orthogonal) projection onto Σ, i.e., P_Σ(x) ∈ argmin_{z∈Σ} ‖x − z‖.

Generalized projected gradient descent (GPGD) for this problem is defined by the iteration
  x_{n+1} = P_Σ(x_n) − μ A^T(A P_Σ(x_n) − y),
where μ > 0 is a step size. Assume A satisfies a restricted isometry property on Σ − Σ and that P_Σ satisfies a restricted Lipschitz property, so that under these hypotheses the GPGD iterates converge linearly to a neighborhood of x̂ whose radius is controlled by ‖e‖ (stable recovery with linear rate).

Define a denoiser f : R^N → R^N by f(x) = P_Σ(x). The classical Regularization by Denoising (RED) iteration with parameter λ ≥ 0 is
  x_{n+1} = x_n − μ [ A^T(A x_n − y) + λ (x_n − f(x_n)) ],
and a modified RED iteration (in which the data-fidelity gradient is evaluated at the denoised point) is
  x_{n+1} = x_n − μ [ A^T(A f(x_n) − y) + λ (x_n − f(x_n)) ].
When λ = 1, modified RED coincides with GPGD; admissible values λ ≠ 1 yield strictly slower linear convergence rates and weaker identifiability guarantees in this analysis, and analogous convergence results for classical RED require still more restrictive hypotheses.

Problem. Identify a theoretical regime — i.e., a class of measurement operators A, model sets Σ, denoisers f, and parameters λ — in which using either the classical RED iteration or the modified RED iteration with some λ ≠ 1 is provably preferable to running GPGD (λ = 1). More precisely, exhibit hypotheses under which a (classical or modified) RED scheme attains a strictly better convergence rate, a strictly better stability/identifiability constant, or recovery guarantees that GPGD provably cannot achieve; or alternatively prove that no such regime exists, so that GPGD always dominates RED under the present hypotheses.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem at the end of the source note, asking for a theoretical justification of RED-type schemes over GPGD. No published resolution was located; the problem appears to remain open.
